categories.main_business_segments: The Kraft Heinz Company operates through two reportable segments: North America and International. The company manufactures and markets food and beverage products including condiments and sauces, cheese and dairy, meals, meats, refreshment beverages, coffee, and other grocery products. Products are organized into six consumer-driven platforms: Taste Elevation, Fast Fresh Meals, Easy Meals Made Better, Real Food Snacking, Flavorful Hydration, and Easy Indulgent Desserts.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes manufacturing and processing facilities worldwide (78 facilities as of December 31, 2022, with 72 owned and 6 leased) to produce food and beverage products. Core technologies include packaging techniques, product-specific processes, and supply chain optimization. The company also employs co-manufacturing arrangements with third parties and uses hedging techniques to manage commodity price volatility. R&D focuses on product innovations, food safety, quality consistency, and process optimization.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Products are sold through chain, wholesale, cooperative, and independent grocery accounts; convenience, value, and club stores; pharmacies; mass merchants; foodservice distributors; and institutions including hotels, restaurants, and hospitals. The company also sells online through e-commerce platforms. Walmart Inc. is the largest customer, representing approximately 21% of net sales in 2022. The five largest customers in North America accounted for approximately 46% of segment net sales, while the five largest in International accounted for approximately 14%.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally with approximately 70% of 2022 net sales generated in the United States and approximately 30% outside the United States. Key international markets include Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, Brazil, Mexico, and various European countries. The company maintains operations in developed and emerging markets, with significant presence in Europe, Latin America, and Asia-Pacific regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kraft Heinz operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the food and beverage supply chain. The company manufactures products from raw commodities (dairy, meat, oils, vegetables, coffee, grains) and packaging materials (resins, cardboard, metals), then distributes finished products to retailers and foodservice customers. The company sources commodities from large international producers and smaller local sellers, and uses co-manufacturing arrangements to supplement internal production capacity.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include driving transformation through consumer-centric innovation, sustainable growth, and operational efficiency. R&D focuses on product innovations and renovations to meet changing consumer needs, world-class food safety and quality, superior product and package performance, and continuous process and supply chain optimization. The company emphasizes sustainability, ethical sourcing, and environmental responsibility while managing inflationary pressures through pricing actions and efficiency gains.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through product sales of food and beverage products sold to retailers, distributors, foodservice operators, and consumers through e-commerce. Revenue is recognized when control of products passes to customers, net of variable consideration including consumer incentives and trade promotions. The company also generates revenue through licensing intellectual property rights, including perpetual licenses for the Kraft and Velveeta brands granted in connection with the Cheese Transaction.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Kraft Heinz competes in a highly competitive food and beverage industry against large national and international companies and numerous local and regional competitors. The company competes with both branded and private label products on the basis of product innovation, price, quality, nutritional value, brand recognition, marketing effectiveness, and ability to satisfy changing consumer preferences. The company is one of the largest food and beverage manufacturers globally with approximately $26.5 billion in net sales in 2022.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Kraft Heinz is a large-cap company with 2022 net sales of approximately $26.5 billion, representing 1.7% growth compared to 2021. Organic net sales grew 9.8% in 2022, driven by higher pricing (13.2 percentage points) that offset unfavorable volume/mix (3.4 percentage points). Net income increased 131.3% to $2.4 billion in 2022 from $1.0 billion in 2021. The company has approximately 37,000 employees globally and maintains significant debt of $20.1 billion as of December 31, 2022.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kraft Heinz emphasizes iconic and emerging brands with long-standing consumer recognition, including Kraft, Heinz, Oscar Mayer, Philadelphia, Lunchables, Velveeta, Maxwell House, and others. The company differentiates through product innovation, quality, convenience, and brand loyalty. The company leverages its scale and agility to deliver consumer-preferred products and packaging, supports sustainability and ethical sourcing, and focuses on meeting evolving consumer preferences for health, wellness, and environmental responsibility while maintaining competitive pricing.
